citation_grounding_failures: H01-A L1: The attached quote supports the untested longer duration but does not state the three-turn sample size per conversation. That detail is supported by F0's separate citation.
H01.notes: A explicitly identifies 2,345 three-turn conversations as the evaluation sample and distinguishes it from benchmark inventory despite the opening wording. B gives the sample but omits the inventory, guideline and strategy counts. The six model-specific pass-rate comparisons establish the cross-language direction.

H02.notes: Both give the exact final subjective and objective comparisons. The final composite pair supports the direction of improvement, but neither states the across-round trend or quantifies the gap. B gives the RAG objective scores without the plateau and complementary-method conclusion. Benchmark-only scope is conveyed in the cited limitations.

H03.notes: A gives only one HarmNet model result. B supplies all six, with the reported model attributions. Neither states the required Ensemble Attack-GA result. A gives AutoAttack results but omits explicit black-box scope. B gives the defense design and static-test results rather than the AutoAttack comparison. Both publish separate outcome rates but do not explain the AutoEvaluation classification rule in a finding or limitation.

H04.notes: The decoding result is model-specific and does not state the broad result about most adversarial prompts. Both preserve single-turn scope and correctly report timeout rates, but omit the H100 and 600-second conditions, so only the single-turn component earns credit. Both give the trade-off direction without the incremental training time.

H05.notes: All nine GCG Avg@5 values match their model and training condition. Both discuss utility for the named models, but neither publishes the full two-part cross-attack comparison, including the Qwen2.5 result. Those facts are not credited solely because some occur in a quote.

H06.notes: The introduction supports the attributed Vicuna variant for both. A supplies the standard-corpus entity count but not its nine types. The separately reported eight extraction labels are task-specific and earn no corpus-type credit. A publishes the numerical-versus-descriptive result and ablation contrasts; B gives the ablation but not the broader contrast. Both explicitly state that cost/time savings were not measured.

H07.notes: Neither publishes the CLINIC benchmark construction requirements. Both qualify the language gradient as an average and support the specialization comparison with the controlled Qwen/II-Medical results and six-model cross-language results. No universal causal claim is credited.

H08.notes: Both identify the complete low-resource tier and explicitly rule out a Yoruba result. The cited model-specific leakage rows give partial privacy evidence, but neither establishes the GPT-4o-mini ranking or the aggregate medical-model pattern. Only B publishes the high-stakes reliability conclusion.
